newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $70 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $70 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were slow near midday Thursday, with light sales reported at $70.00 per cwt, steady with sales earlier this week, feedlot sources said.

About 4,400 head were sold in Kansas this morning, bringing the week to date tally there to 58,000, USDA said. No sales were reported in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, by USDA or cattle feeders.
The bulk of this week's sales occured Monday through Wednesday, with most feedlots said to be current in their marketings.
In the Texas Panhandle, there were 89,700 head sold for the week to date as of early Thursday, including 17,200 formulated cattle and 2,800 contracts to be shipped this week, according to USDA.
Boxed beef sales at midday were moderate, although packers were still cutting prices to keep product flowing, market sources said.
Beef was quoted by USDA down $0.21 to $0.66 per cwt, with 158 fabricated loads reported sold.
